1: Paul thanks God that their faith and love keep growing during persecution. God is just: he will give relief to the afflicted and repay those who afflict them when the Lord Jesus is revealed.
Suffering for the faith is not a sign that God has abandoned us. Justice will be done.
2: Some claimed the day of the Lord had already arrived. Paul says a rebellion and "the man of lawlessness" must come first, and the Lord will destroy him. Meanwhile, stand firm and hold to the traditions taught by word of mouth or by letter.
Paul puts oral teaching beside written teaching. This is one basis for the Catholic regard for Tradition alongside Scripture.
3: Some believers had stopped working and were meddling in others' affairs. Paul points to his own example of labour and gives the rule: anyone unwilling to work should not eat. Do not grow tired of doing good.
Waiting for the Lord is no excuse for idleness. Ordinary work is part of a holy life.
